# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 64 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 47-48 | Coptic

---

## Saying 64

Jesus said: "A man had guests coming. When he had prepared the dinner, he sent his servant to invite the guests. He went to the first and said: 'My master invites you.' He said: 'I have claims against some merchants; they are coming to me tonight. I am going to give them instructions. Please excuse me from the dinner.' He went to another and said: 'My master has invited you.' He said: 'I have bought a house and I am needed there for a day. I will have no time.' He went to another and said: 'My master invites you.' He said: 'A friend of mine is getting married, and I am in charge of the banquet. I cannot come. Please excuse me from the dinner.' He went to another and said: 'My master invites you.' He said: 'I have bought an estate. I am going to collect the rent. I cannot come. Please excuse me.' The servant returned and said to his master: 'Those whom you invited to dinner have asked to be excused.' The master said to his servant: 'Go out to the roads and bring whoever you find, that they may dine.' Traders and merchants shall not enter the places of my Father."

---

**Translator's Notes (LOGOS):**

- "Claims against merchants" — first excuse involves a financial dispute, not merely suppliers coming
- "Estate" for farm — the economic register is elevated
- "In charge of the banquet" — the third guest's social responsibility is made explicit
- The final condemnation: "Traders and merchants" — two classes of commercial operators
